exposure: study period (first 4 years vs. last 4 years)
cohort: The study included 2742 women attending a tertiary hospital for contraceptive preferences over an eight-year period.
finding: Coitus interruptus was found to be the prevailing contraceptive method across all age groups, despite an overall increase in birth control method use attributed to increased education and access to sexual health services.
cross-section timing: Data was collected over an 8-year period, divided into two 4-year segments (Group I and Group II).
